subject: Is "stan" promising for fitting my model?

messages.author: 4e6e00f7b64d9dff
messages.subject: Is "stan" promising for fitting my model?
parts:
Is this the right forum for describing a HBM to see whether Stan might help me fit it?

I've written single-site update MCMC code using C++ to fit a very basic version of the model (a fairly simple model), and after 3 million iterations, the chain hasn't moved noticeably.  The parameters I'm trying to estimate are daily animal locations, which means there's an incredible amount of autocorrelation.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Is "stan" promising for fitting my model?
parts:
On Friday, October 10, 2014 3:32:41 PM UTC-4, Margaret Short wrote:
Is this the right forum for describing a HBM to see whether Stan might help me fit it?

I've written single-site update MCMC code using C++ to fit a very basic version of the model (a fairly simple model), and after 3 million iterations, the chain hasn't moved noticeably.  The parameters I'm trying to estimate are daily animal locations, which means there's an incredible amount of autocorrelation.

Stan has a good chance of fitting any model, as long as the parameter space is continuous or you can marginalize the discrete unknowns. I certainly would have tried Stan before writing a custom MCMC sampler.

Ben
